title: “To Preserve Our Freedoms, We Must Defend Mexico’s Sovereignty”
author: Nancy Flores
content:
_This article by[Nancy
Flores](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/nancy_contra/) originally appeared
in the [September 15, 2026 edition of
Contralinea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/para-preservar-
nuestras-libertades-hay-que-defender-la-soberania-de-mexico/), one of Mexico's
leading investigative journalism outlets._

The construction of a full, plural, and inclusive democracy --based on a
national project with social justice-- also depends, states President Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo in her Second Government Report, on a clear awareness:

> To preserve our freedoms, we must defend national sovereignty.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Government Report

Throughout the **1,344-page document** , it sets out the progress of that
pursuit of sovereignty in strategic sectors, beginning with the defense of the
homeland's territory, not only as the basis of national security but above all
in the face of the open and covert pressures of foreign interests. To this is
added consolidation in the energy, food, financial, commercial, health,
scientific, technological, and even satellite areas.

In her accountability report, the president highlights that the change of
mentality among the people has made possible what she calls a "historic
political and social transformation that Mexico is [currently] living
through." She also notes that hope has flourished of building a nation for all
--with a well-being State benefiting the majority of Mexican women and men--
and not one at the service of the elite that governed during the _prianismo_
(the PRI-PAN era).

She observes that the change of regime, which separates economic power from
political power, is based on a government at the service of the people, one
that fights corruption and continues republican austerity. It is worth
recalling that under President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, **13.4 million
people rose out of poverty, and 1.7 million out of extreme poverty**.

> The most tangible achievement of this process is the reduction of poverty
> and inequality, which had reached historic levels caused by four decades of
> neoliberal policies that privatized rights and the nation's resources and
> concentrated national wealth in a few hands.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Government Report

Regarding the new social pact, the document states that it is based on
economic and social policies that drive development with well-being, social
justice, and sustainability, drawing on public and private investment. And so,
Sheinbaum Pardo's commitment, it adds, is to keep governing "in favor of the
collective interest, with honesty, with democracy and citizen participation,
with efficiency and a humanist vision."

## Territorial Sovereignty and National Security

The president's Second Report explains that, on national security, defense,
and sovereignty, the government applies a "comprehensive strategy to safeguard
peace, public order, and the integrity of the population, articulating the
operational capabilities of the Army, the Mexican Air Force, the National
Guard, and the Navy of Mexico to strengthen territorial deployment, the
prevention of and fight against crime, as well as the consolidation of
strategic infrastructure that increases the State's response capacity."

It details that Mexico's armed institutions are robust and modern, capable of
effectively detecting, preventing, and neutralizing threats that compromise
the integrity, independence, and sovereignty of the nation. "To this end, the
Armed Forces maintained high standards of personnel training; continued the
surveillance and protection of the airspace, national seas, and strategic
facilities; maintained a permanent deployment of Army, Air Force, Navy, and
National Guard personnel to deter drug trafficking and contain criminal
activity against the country; and strengthened their operational, strategic,
technological, intelligence, and cyberdefense capabilities." On this last
point, it adds that the Navy of Mexico's cyberdefense capabilities were
consolidated, "as a key dimension for the protection of sovereignty and the
institutional environment."

Specifically on the bilateral relationship with the United States, the
document states that it was strengthened through political dialogue and
institutional coordination, always under the principles of respect for
sovereignty, mutual trust, shared responsibility, and cooperation without
subordination. "Follow-up was given to the main high-level dialogue spaces,
including more than 17 calls between President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo and
President Donald J. Trump, as well as meetings with cabinet members, state
governments, and the U.S. Congress, which helped advance cooperation and
understanding on priority issues of the bilateral agenda, such as security,
migration, border infrastructure, regional competitiveness, and the protection
of Mexican communities abroad."

Regarding cooperation on security, the document says that "the actions carried
out between September 1, 2025, and August 15, 2026, were conducted in
accordance with the constitutional principles that guide Mexico's foreign
policy, strengthening an agenda oriented toward technical dialogue,
information exchange, and the building of institutional understanding."

Reference is also made to the commitments of the Bilateral Implementation
Group and of the Cooperation Program on Border Security and Law Enforcement;
these included actions to combat illicit finances, fuel trafficking, and
extortion, as well as customs exchange and the handling of new threats, though
it does not specify which. It adds that Operation Firewall (_Cortafuegos_)
continued in order to strengthen investigations linked to arms trafficking.

## Financial Sovereignty

On this point of financial sovereignty, the Report indicates that it has
already been demonstrated that one can govern with social justice without
compromising the stability of the national finances. "As of the second quarter
of 2026, the debt of the federal public sector, measured through the historic
balance of the public sector's financing requirements, stood at **51 percent
of GDP** , 1.6 percent less than at the close of 2025."

On that downward trajectory of public debt, it explains that it was achieved
without sacrificing social investment or the country's strategic
infrastructure. This, the document states, "is the most conclusive proof that
republican austerity is a responsible State policy that strengthens Mexico's
financial sovereignty in the face of international volatility. Within the
framework of these measures, fiscal savings of 106.8 million pesos were
generated in the Federal Public Administration, resources that are redirected
directly to the well-being of the people."

## Commercial Sovereignty

With the aim of facilitating more competitive, secure, and sustainable trade,
strengthening commercial sovereignty, and raising operational efficiency, the
Second Government Report explains that work was done to strengthen rail
freight transport. This, it adds, will increase the volume of goods moved and
improve national logistics competitiveness.

In this regard, it reports that the National Railway System has 29,042
kilometers of track and, from January to June 2026, moved 30.2 million
passengers and 65.3 million tons of cargo. "In this context, the rail works
for passenger trains registered progress on the strategic corridors Mexico
City-Pachuca, Mexico City-Queretaro, Queretaro-Irapuato, and Saltillo-Nuevo
Laredo, while the studies for the trains between Queretaro, San Luis Potosi,
and Saltillo, as well as the train between Irapuato and Guadalajara, are in
their final stage of development."

## Food Sovereignty

Another area highlighted is that of food sovereignty. In that sense, it
indicates that an agenda is being promoted to drive resilient and sustainable
agri-food systems, with rural justice. To that end, technological solutions
are being developed together with traditional knowledge, to strengthen the
cultivation of corn and beans, with better productivity, resilience, and
sustainability.

"The project is led by SECIHTI, in coordination with the Secretariat of
Agriculture and Rural Development and the National Institute of Forestry,
Agricultural and Livestock Research. Among the main results: more than 70 tons
of native and improved seeds were delivered to nearly 5,000 small- and medium-
scale producers, and a national inventory of machinery and water technologies
was carried out, which will be validated during 2026 and 2027. Finally, an
agroecological transition model was validated in the states of Chiapas,
Veracruz, Jalisco, and Chihuahua, demonstrating an increase of at least 20
percent in the yield and profitability of corn and bean production," the
Second Government Report details.

## Energy Sovereignty

On consolidating energy sovereignty, the document adds that the aim is to
"guarantee the reliable supply of electricity and fuels, expand strategic
infrastructure, and accelerate the transition toward renewable sources. To
this end, constitutional, legal, and regulatory reforms were promoted that
strengthened the sector's public companies."

It also notes that "the axes of this policy were the recovery of the State's
stewardship and the establishment of binding planning that articulates
decisions on investment, regulation, and infrastructure development with
national objectives and needs. In this way, this model guides the growth of
the energy system under criteria of sovereignty, self-sufficiency, security,
and justice, guaranteeing the supply, continuity, accessibility, reliability,
and sustainability of energy for people and productive activities."

Specifically, it adds that in the area of hydrocarbons a comprehensive
exploration strategy is applied with new technologies, subsoil studies, and
the incorporation of new areas with oil potential, in order to increase the
replacement of reserves.

"Between September 2025 and June 2026, **eight new exploratory wells** were
authorized, six of which began drilling activities with programmed depths of
up to 8,482 meters. These operations made it possible to expand geological
knowledge of the national subsoil, reduce exploratory uncertainty in areas
with hydrocarbon potential, generate fundamental technical information to
update knowledge of the subsoil, confirm new exploratory opportunities, and
support the planning of future projects."

## Health and Scientific Sovereignty

To guarantee health sovereignty, the Second Report indicates that molecular
epidemiological surveillance systems for respiratory diseases are being
consolidated, research into neurodegenerative diseases is being strengthened,
and studies on healthy aging, frailty, dementias, and cardiometabolic diseases
are being expanded. With these actions, priority groups are being served in
order to reduce gaps in health.

The document states that "the country's health autonomy and national capacity
for the production of medicines, vaccines, medical devices, and health
supplies were also strengthened through the streamlining of health procedures,
the attraction of strategic investments, and the promotion of technology
transfer, within the framework of Plan Mexico. Memoranda of understanding were
signed with international companies to strengthen productive capacities in
strategic sectors and foster clinical research, among which the technology-
transfer agreement to begin national production of messenger RNA (mRNA)
vaccines against COVID-19 stands out."

In this area it is also highlighted that the Secretariat of Health formalized
agreements with international laboratories to encourage local production of
strategic medicines, as well as to install plants for active pharmaceutical
ingredients. This seeks to strengthen national manufacturing capacities and
the country's health sovereignty.

Likewise, it indicates that "improvements were registered in national
capacities for technological innovation through the development of patents,
medical technologies, rehabilitation devices, diagnostic tools, and precision-
medicine solutions. These advances helped drive technology transfer,
strengthen national scientific sovereignty, and expand institutional
capacities to respond to priority public health problems."

On the national policy of science, humanities, technology, and innovation, it
explains that its objective is to guarantee the right of all people to benefit
from scientific, humanistic, and technological development. "The human right
to science guides the actions and strategies aimed at broadening access to
knowledge, strengthening the capacities for critical thinking, and promoting
that the population has the elements to participate in an informed manner in
decision-making. This policy is oriented toward strengthening national
capacities and building technological sovereignty with a social focus. Among
its main strategies are the training and consolidation of the scientific,
humanistic, and technological community, as well as the promotion of the
development of priority technologies through maturation and scaling processes
that address regional and national needs."

Advances in space sovereignty are also set out. In this regard, the Second
Government Report notes that, on June 4, 2026, the Mexican Space Program
2026-2030 was published in the Official Gazette (DOF), "a planning instrument
to order the country's space policy and articulate projects of connectivity,
satellite observation, technological development, and space sovereignty. With
it, a path was established to move from a model centered on the use of space
technology to one oriented toward the development of national capabilities."
